headline: Today's 21 km at easy pace and low effort marks the return of longer time-on-feet the strain flag was waiting for.
confidence_reasons: Multiple data sources active in last 3 days
summary:
The long-ish easy run you'd been missing has now landed. Today's effort was your longest single run in this block and sat at a controlled, low ATE — exactly the kind of session that should quietly resolve the strain-ratio artefact flagged earlier in the week. This is durability work reappearing, not a spike, and it slots cleanly into the consolidation you've been running.

Your aerobic picture continues to hold together well: easy-run HR remains meaningfully lower than the prior comparable period, strength frequency has doubled into this block, and volume is climbing modestly rather than lurching. That combination is the signature of a base that's deepening rather than plateauing. Nothing here suggests you've lost anything — the lower recent intensity is a deliberate feature of the last week, not evidence of decline.

What's still absent is anything that rehearses the specific demands of St. Olavsleden — pack load, back-to-back running, and sustained climbing. Today's elevation was modest and this was a single run, not a double day. With the crossing now well inside a month, that gap is the thing worth closing, though the general aerobic and structural readiness you're carrying is a strong platform to build it on.
watch_items: Whether this longer run pulls the strain ratio back up, confirming the earlier dip was a rolling-average artefact.
Whether pack-loaded or back-to-back running finally appears, given how close the self-supported crossing now is.
Whether per-run elevation starts climbing to rehearse the sustained border-section terrain.
Whether the recent erratic nights settle into something steadier now that longer sessions are re-entering the week.

evidence_items.text: ▼ Easy-run HR averaging 142 bpm vs 153 bpm prior period (comparable-effort runs, 8 vs 8 runs)
▲ 4-week volume 152 km vs 137 km prior block (+11%)
▲ Zone 2: 187 min vs 180-240 min/week target (104% of minimum); grey zone (Z3+Z4): 1.6%
